predecessors.note: In 617 officers at Baling Commandery recruited Xiao Xian, a descendant of the Western Liang's Xiao Cha; he became Duke of Liang at Luochuan (Xiao Xian page; Western Liang page: he 'occupied the former Western Liang territory and others').

land.text: 'most of modern Hubei, Hunan, Guangxi, and northern Vietnam': east to Jiujiang, west to the Three Gorges, south to Jiaozhi (Hanoi), north to the Han River

successors.note: Li Xiaogong's assault came in winter 621; Xiao surrendered at Jiangling and was beheaded at Chang'an.

capitals.name: Baling (Yueyang)
capitals.note: 'He first ruled from Baling.' Yueyang is near the commandery, the researcher's reading.

capitals.name: Jiangling (Jingzhou)
capitals.note: Moved there after his general Yang Daosheng captured Jiangling (after summer 618).

rulers.name: Xiao Xian
rulers.note: Duke of Liang 617, Prince of Liang in winter 617, emperor in summer 618.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 617: the first base at Baling and Luochuan, northern Hunan, before the Yangtze and the south came over.

union.text: Yuzhang (Nanchang), taken from Lin Shihong by Su Hu'er around the new year 618

correction.text: 'most of modern Hubei, Hunan, Guangxi, and northern Vietnam': east to Jiujiang, west to the Three Gorges, south to Jiaozhi (Hanoi), north to the Han River

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 618-621: 'his state covered most of modern Hubei, Hunan, Guangxi, and northern Vietnam', with 'more than 400,000 regular soldiers'. Guangxi and northern Vietnam were mostly not conquered: Sui officials 'largely surrendered' after Emperor Yang's death. No area on the page. [Reviewer ea-03-f, 2026-10-19: Yuzhang (Nanchang, 100 km) added to the correction and to the 621 dissolve region: the ledger's 618 gain from lin-shihong-s-chu had no trace in the keyframes and lin-shihong-s-chu_618 drops it, so the plain was drawn for nobody; the Xiao Xian page has his territory reach 'as far east as Jiujiang']

ledger.note: 617: Xiao Xian rises as Duke of Liang. 'In 617, military officers at Baling Commandery (near modern Yueyang)' recruited him as county magistrate of Luochuan; Prince of Liang in winter 617; the Transition page has Liang 'by 617' to 621.

618: Xiao Xian takes Hubei, Guangxi and northern Vietnam. He took the imperial title in summer 618; his general Yang Daosheng captured Jiangling afterwards; after Emperor Yang's death in spring 618 Sui officials in Guangxi and northern Vietnam 'largely surrendered'. The page gives no month.

region.text: Yuzhang, Lin Shihong's capital, and its plain

ledger.note: 618: Su Hu'er takes Yuzhang from Lin Shihong. 'Around new year 618, his general Su Hu'er captured Lin's major city Yuzhang (Nanchang), and Lin retreated' (the Lin Shihong page: Lin then retreated to Yugan).
618: the capital moves from Baling to Jiangling after Yang Daosheng takes it (the page puts this after summer 618).

union.text: Yuzhang (Nanchang), taken from Lin Shihong by Su Hu'er around the new year 618

region.text: 'most of modern Hubei, Hunan, Guangxi, and northern Vietnam': east to Jiujiang, west to the Three Gorges, south to Jiaozhi (Hanoi), north to the Han River

ledger.note: 621: Li Xiaogong ends the Liang. 'A major Tang assault came in winter 621, led by Li Xiaogong with Li Jing assisting'; Xiao surrendered at Jiangling ('Only Xiao Xian should die. The people are innocent') and was taken to Chang'an and beheaded.

wars.name: Tang conquest of Xiao Xian's Liang
wars.outcome: Tang victory: Jiangling besieged and Xiao Xian surrendered in winter 621.
wars.note: The Transition page names the Tang commanders Li Xiaogong and Li Jing's assault the same year.

certainty.note: A province-span realm; Guangxi and the Hanoi region were nominal; no boundary is given.

sources.title: Xiao Xian
sources.note: Rise at Baling 617, titles, capitals, Hubei-Hunan-Guangxi-northern Vietnam, Lin Shihong, the winter 621 Tang assault and surrender.

sources.title: Transition from Sui to Tang
sources.note: The southern Liang 'by 617' to 621, based at Jiangling.

notes: REBEL STATE. A second 'Liang' of the same age is Liang Shidu's (liang-shidu-s-liang). Xiao Xian is a great-grandson of the Western Liang's Xiao Cha according to the Western Liang page. The Hanoi region and Guangxi are in the span only because Sui officials 'largely surrendered' (Xiao Xian page); Cliopatria's Early Ly and Champa rows are not involved. Shen Faxing's Liang south of the Yangtze (c. 619-620, Transition page) is not written.
